notes.coptic_form: ϣⲁⲣⲉ ⲡⲟⲩⲉ ⲡⲟⲩⲉ ⲝⲓ ϣⲃ̄ⲓⲱ ⲕⲁⲧⲁ ⲛⲉϩⲍⲃⲏⲩⲉ
notes.decision: Translated as the maxim 'each one receives recompense according to his works' — habitual ϣⲁⲣⲉ + ⲝⲓ (Lyc. ϫⲓ) 'receive' + ϣⲃ̄ⲓⲱ 'recompense' + ⲕⲁⲧⲁ + ⲛⲉϩ-ϩⲃⲏⲩⲉ 'his works.' This is the principle the disciple cites against the efficacy of intercessory prayer — and which the Apostle's reply will reconcile with cosmic prayer.

notes.coptic_form: ⲟⲩⲛⲁⲃ ⲧⲟⲛⲱ ⲡⲉ ϩⲧⲁⲓⲁⲓⲧ ⲛⲁⲍⲣⲛ ⲛ̄ⲣⲱⲙⲉ
notes.decision: Rendered ⲧⲟⲛⲱ as 'weighty matter' per accumulated vocabulary entry (which notes ⲧⲟⲛⲱ as substantival 'raising-up' = 'weighty/momentous thing'). The qualitative ϩⲧⲁⲓⲁⲓⲧ I read as Lyc. reflex of ⲧⲁⲩⲏⲩ 'has been proclaimed/sent forth' (qualitative of ⲧⲁⲩⲟ 'proclaim'); fits the discourse since the disciple is asking about a saying he has heard. Alternative reading: stative of ⲁⲓⲁⲓ 'multiply' = 'has grown great' is also plausible.

Greek προσχαρίζομαι 'grant in addition' — distinguished from simple ⲭⲁⲣⲓⲍⲉ in line 18. The προσ- prefix is theologically significant: when one prays for another, the granting is supererogatory (in addition to the regular reckoning). This reconciles the maxim of line 9 with the efficacy of intercessory prayer.

Translated 'this prayer came into being from the firsts' — ⲛ̄ⲧⲍⲟⲩⲓⲧⲉ from ⲡⲍⲟⲩⲓ̈ⲧ 'the foremost/first' (in glossary). The Apostle grounds prayer's efficacy in cosmogonic precedence: prayer's reality comes from the original cosmic beings.

'(The Church) which bears the flesh' — Greek φορεῖ 'wear, bear (as garment).' The Church-on-earth is characterized as the flesh-bearing community, distinguishing it from the cosmic divine assemblies but parallel in its prayer-function.

Final-line verbs all 3sg.f perfect, subject = the Mother of Life from line 29-30. The triple sequence beseeched/glorified/blessed (with restored ⲁⲥⲁⲓⲧⲓ 'requested,' ⲁⲥϣⲗⲏⲛ 'prayed' preceding) gives the Mother's fivefold cosmogonic prayer-act — paralleling the gods' first prayer in line 21 and grounding the teaching that all prayer descends from primordial divine prayer.
